sections.learningObjectives:
- Define the word parts (roots, prefixes, and suffixes) for the cardiovascular, lymphatic, and immune systems.
- Build and decode medical terms for the heart, blood vessels, blood, lymphatic system, and immune system.
- Recognize common cardiovascular, lymphatic, and immune conditions and procedures by their terminology.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of "cardio" like the cardio exercise you do to work out your heart. The word part "cardi/o" is a secret code for the heart.

### Question 2

Your body has little tubes, like straws, that carry blood everywhere. Those tubes are called vessels, and "angi/o" and "vas/o" both mean those tubes.

### Question 3

"Hem/o" is the code for blood. That's why a doctor who studies blood is called a hematologist.

### Question 4

Veins are the tubes that carry blood back to your heart. "Phleb/o" and "ven/o" are two different code words for those same tubes.

### Question 5

Arteries are the tubes that carry blood from your heart out to the rest of your body. "Arteri/o" is the code word for them.

### Question 6

"Endo" means inside. The endocardium is the smooth layer on the inside of your heart, like the inside wall of a house.

### Question 7

Red blood cells are like little delivery trucks that carry oxygen. "Erythrocyte" literally means "red cell."

### Question 8

A thrombus is like a clump that forms in your blood. "Thromb/o" is the code for that clump.

### Question 9

Lymph nodes are little filters that catch germs. "Lymphaden/o" is the code for those filters.

### Question 10

Your spleen is an organ that helps filter your blood and fight germs. "Splen/o" is its code word.

### Question 11

"Immun/o" is the code for your body's defense team, the part that protects you from germs.

### Question 12

"-ectomy" means "cut out and take away." A tonsillectomy is when a doctor takes out the tonsils.

### Question 13

"Hyper" means "too much" or "way up high." Hypertension is blood pressure that is running too high.

### Question 14

"-megaly" means "grew too big." Cardiomegaly means the heart got bigger than normal.

### Question 15

Tachycardia is a heart that races. A resting pulse of 118 is like the heart sprinting while sitting still, so it is tachycardia.

### Question 16

Hypertension is blood pressure running too high, like a garden hose under too much pressure. A reading of 150/95 is too high.

### Question 17

"Hypo" means "too little." Hypotension is blood pressure that has dropped too low, like a hose with weak water flow.

### Question 18

The inside of your heart has a smooth lining. "Endo" = inside, "-itis" = inflamed, so endocarditis is that inside lining getting sore and swollen.

### Question 19

Your heart sits inside a protective bag. "Peri" means "around," so pericarditis is that bag getting inflamed.

### Question 20

Your heart is a muscle. "My/o" = muscle, "-itis" = inflamed, so myocarditis is a sore, inflamed heart muscle.

### Question 21

Atherosclerosis is like gunk building up inside a pipe so water flows poorly. That gunk is fatty plaque.

### Question 22

Think of arteriosclerosis as any pipe getting stiff. Atherosclerosis is one specific reason: fatty gunk (plaque) stuck inside the pipe.

### Question 23

A vein gets sore and swollen, and a little clot forms inside it. "Thromb" = clot, "phleb" = vein, "-itis" = inflamed.

### Question 24

If you bump your arm and it swells into a purple bruise, that pooled blood under the skin is a hematoma — a "blood lump."

### Question 25

Red blood cells carry oxygen like little delivery trucks. Too few trucks (low hemoglobin) leaves the body tired — that is anemia.

### Question 26

White blood cells are your body's germ-fighting soldiers. "Leuk/o" = white, "-penia" = too few, so leukopenia means too few soldiers.

### Question 27

When you have an infection, your body makes extra germ-fighting cells. "-cytosis" means "more cells," so leukocytosis means more white cells.

### Question 28

Platelets are like sticky patches that stop bleeding. "Thromb/o" = clotting cell, "-penia" = too few, so thrombocytopenia means too few patches.

### Question 29

Leukemia is when the body's white-cell factory goes haywire and makes too many broken germ-fighting cells.

### Question 30

When a lymph node swells and gets sore because it is fighting germs, that is lymphadenitis — an angry little filter.

### Question 31

"-pathy" means "disease of." Lymphadenopathy means the lymph nodes are diseased, and often that shows up as swollen glands.

### Question 32

"-oma" means a growth or lump. A lymphangioma is a harmless lump made of lymph-vessel tissue.

### Question 33

Lymphoma is cancer of the lymph system's cells. Hodgkin lymphoma is one well-known type.

### Question 34

The spleen is an organ that filters blood. "-megaly" means "grew too big," so splenomegaly means a too-big spleen.

### Question 35

Your tonsils are two lumps at the back of your throat. When they get sore and swollen from a cold, that's tonsillitis.

### Question 36

Lymph fluid normally drains away like water down a drain. If the drain clogs, the area puffs up — that swelling is lymphedema.

### Question 37

Lymph vessels are tiny drainage tubes. Lymphangitis is when those tubes get inflamed, sometimes showing as a red streak under the skin.

### Question 38

Ischemia is like a hose being kinked so a part of the body doesn't get enough oxygen. It's the "low supply" step before damage.

### Question 39

Your heart normally beats in a steady pattern, like a drum. An arrhythmia is when that drumbeat gets out of pattern.

### Question 40

An aneurysm is like a weak spot in a bicycle tire that balloons outward. If it bursts, it is a medical emergency.

### Question 41

A thrombus is a clot stuck in place. If it breaks off and floats downstream to block a new spot, it becomes an embolus.

### Question 42

In hemophilia, the blood's "glue" that stops bleeding is missing or weak, so a small cut can bleed for a long time.

### Question 43

Think of an antigen as a "wanted" poster for a germ, and the antibody as the special key that locks onto it so it can be removed.

### Question 44

Immunoglobulins are the body's custom-made keys that lock onto specific germs. They are the proteins we call antibodies.

### Question 45

Anaphylaxis is the body's alarm system going off all at once — throat swelling, trouble breathing — and it needs emergency help right away.

### Question 46

Usually your immune system only attacks invaders. In autoimmune disease, it gets confused and attacks your own body, like friendly fire.

### Question 47

"Deficiency" means "not enough." Immunodeficiency means the body's defense team is too weak to fight germs well.

### Question 48

Hematocrit is like measuring how much of a smoothie is fruit versus liquid — it's the share of your blood that is red cells.

### Question 49

A heart attack is when a part of the heart muscle doesn't get blood and starts to die. Crushing chest pain is a classic warning sign.

### Question 50

If the heart pump gets weak, fluid can back up like a clogged drain, causing swelling and shortness of breath. That backup is the "congestion."

### Question 51

A heart attack is a plumbing problem (a blocked pipe). Cardiac arrest is an electrical problem — the heart's pump stops entirely.

### Question 52

The heart has its own special supply pipes called coronary arteries. When those pipes get clogged, the heart muscle gets less fuel.

### Question 53

Angina is the heart's warning signal that it isn't getting enough oxygen, like a cramp when a muscle works too hard.

### Question 54

Varicose veins are bulging, ropey veins under the skin where blood pools instead of flowing back up to the heart.

### Question 55

Sitting still a long time can let a clot form in a deep leg vein. The dangerous part is that the clot could break loose and travel to the lungs, so the doctor must be told right away.

### Question 56

A stroke is a "brain attack" — a part of the brain suddenly loses its blood supply, like a power outage in one room.

### Question 57

Mono is a virus that tires the body out and swells the lymph nodes, often called the "kissing disease" because it spreads through saliva.

### Question 58

HIV is the germ that sneaks in and weakens the body's defense team. If it weakens them enough, the person reaches a stage called AIDS.

### Question 59

Hodgkin lymphoma is one kind of lymph-system cancer, named after the doctor who described it. It has a special abnormal cell that shows up under a microscope.

### Question 60

An EKG is like a graph of the heart's electric beat, showing whether the rhythm is steady.

### Question 61

An echocardiogram uses sound waves, like a bat's echolocation, to make a moving picture of the heart.

### Question 62

An angiogram is like putting dye into pipes and taking an X-ray to see where they are narrowed or blocked.

### Question 63

Angioplasty is like pushing a small balloon through a clogged pipe and inflating it to open the passage back up.

### Question 64

A cardiac catheter is a skinny tube sent up to the heart like a tiny plumber's camera to look for and fix blockages.

### Question 65

CABG is like building a detour road around a blocked highway so traffic (blood) can still get through.

### Question 66

Phlebotomy is the careful poke of a needle into a vein to collect blood for testing — what people call "having blood drawn."

### Question 67

A CBC is like a census of the blood, counting all the different kinds of cells to make sure there are the right amounts.

### Question 68

A blood pressure cuff (sphygmomanometer) measures how hard the blood is pushing. A very high number should be checked again and told to the doctor right away, not ignored.

### Question 69

"-ectomy" means "take out." A splenectomy is when the spleen is surgically removed.

### Question 70

A tonsillectomy is the operation that takes out the tonsils, often because they keep getting infected.

### Question 71

A lymphadenectomy is when a surgeon removes lymph nodes, often to check for or treat cancer.

### Question 72

Chest pain can mean the heart is in trouble. The right move is to quickly call for help from the doctor or nurse, like pulling a fire alarm.

### Question 73

Drawing blood is a careful, skilled job. Only people who have been trained and given permission may do it, and they must always be safe and clean.
